title: Normalized compact-support exchanges commute with coefficient passage
statement: Fix $D,\ell,\Omega,X_0,Y_0,f_0,c_0$ as in [def-coef-verdier-weil-data]. Given an actual duality $B_X$ with its internal-Hom and exceptional-unit dualizing identifications [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data], one can choose $B_Y$ with the same identifications, a coefficient Weil-duality record $W_Y$ on $B_Y$ satisfying DualizingNormalization, and an actual exceptional system $A$ with its exceptional-duality formula. For every coefficient Weil-duality records $W_X,W_Y$ on these dualities there are left Frobenius exchange isomorphisms with the finite and common canonical realization normalizations, and their finite-scalar and stage-inclusion squares commute on all underlying objects. The statement is existential in the exceptional system: its realization isomorphisms and coefficient comparisons are chosen together from the normalized construction. It asserts no right Frobenius exchange or Weil unit/counit equation.

proof.text: Use the normalized construction of [thm-coef-qbar-verdier] and [thm-coef-rational-verdier] to choose the relative exceptional system and its exceptional-duality formula from the same coefficient models. Keep its coherent finite compact-support realizations. Conjugate the canonical rational exchange by these realizations. Its inverse exists by [lem-coef-frobenius-exchange-equivalence], and conjugating back gives the finite normalization.

Choose $B_Y$ by the same normalized construction, with the natural Koszul signed symmetry at every finite field. The one-scheme argument of [lem-coef-weil-normalized-duality] applies to this $B_Y$: the inverse-Frobenius pullbacks are equivalences [lem-pod-isomorphism-field-transport], the structure-morphism mate [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] on the coefficient unit gives the dualizing structure, and the evaluation-normalized internal-Hom comparison [lem-pod-geometric-frobenius-internal-hom-comparison] with the injective transpose [lem-coef-completed-tensor-hom-transpose] gives $W_Y$ with its dualizing normalization.

The whole-system scalar/exchange square of [def-weil-operation-exchange-coefficient-descent] commutes before taking inverse limit and localization. Conjugate this square by the scalar-normalized realizations of A to obtain the displayed finite scalar equation, including identity inclusions.

Descend the exchanges and their inverses through the prescribed left-inclusion comparisons of A. A common-stage arrow is represented at a common finite field [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]; the scalar equation proves independence and naturality. Their component formula agrees with the canonical commonStageExchange. Substituting the stageNormalized components of W_X and W_Y gives the stage square.

theorem coef_weil_left_exchange_compatibility
    (c₀ : Compactification f₀.left) (BX : FiberDuality D l hl Ω X₀)
    (hIX : Nonempty (FiberInternalHom D l hl Ω X₀ BX))
    (hωX : FiberDualizing D l hl Ω X₀ BX) :
    ∃ (BY : FiberDuality D l hl Ω Y₀)
      (A : FiberExceptional D l hl Ω X₀ f₀
        (FrobeniusExchange.geometricCompactification D f₀ c₀)),
      Nonempty (FiberInternalHom D l hl Ω Y₀ BY) ∧
      FiberDualizing D l hl Ω Y₀ BY ∧
      Nonempty (FiberExceptionalFormula D l hl Ω X₀ f₀
        (FrobeniusExchange.geometricCompactification D f₀ c₀) BX BY A) ∧
      (∃ WY : Coefficients D l hl Ω Y₀ BY, DualizingNormalization D l hl Ω Y₀ BY WY) ∧
      ∀ (WX : Coefficients D l hl Ω X₀ BX) (WY : Coefficients D l hl Ω Y₀ BY),
        Nonempty (LeftExchanges D l hl Ω X₀ f₀ c₀ A WX WY)
